# **Autonomous Generative Manufacturing Platform for High-Performance Complex Geometry Optimization**

## **1\. Identification and Significance of the Proposed Innovation**

### **1.1 The Manufacturing Bottleneck in Complex Geometry Optimization**

Modern high-performance engineering sectors—spanning extreme-performance motocross, professional powersports, and advanced subsea propulsion—rely heavily on components with highly complex, multi-physics geometries. Internal fluid channels, optimized thermal cooling pathways, and electromagnetic keep-outs (such as Halbach array motor housings) dictate performance limits. However, the traditional software toolchain for designing and manufacturing these components remains fundamentally bottlenecked by legacy Computer-Aided Design (CAD) architectures based on boundary-representation (B-rep) geometry.  
B-rep CAD represents objects via explicit surface boundaries stitched together mathematically. While effective for simple prismatic parts, B-rep systems catastrophically fail when subjected to automated, iterative artificial intelligence (AI) design loops. As an AI swarm or optimization algorithm mutates internal geometry to optimize fluid dynamics or structural load paths, minor topological changes frequently result in non-manifold edges, self-intersecting surfaces, and boolean processing failures. Consequently, engineering teams spend weeks manually repairing parametric models, rendering closed-loop autonomous optimization practically impossible.

### **1.2 The ScanIQ Computational Voxel Paradigm**

ScanIQ solves this structural limitation by replacing B-rep CAD with a native computational manufacturing platform driven by implicit voxel mathematics and Signed Distance Fields (SDF). Rather than manipulating fragile surface boundaries, ScanIQ’s core engine evaluates volumetric data programmatically.  
In an implicit voxel framework, every point in space is mapped to a signed distance relative to the nearest geometric boundary. This architecture guarantees absolute topological robustness: boolean operations (union, intersection, subtraction) and morphological transformations (erosion, dilation, offset keep-outs) are executed mathematically on scalar fields. Regardless of how drastically an AI agent mutates internal fluid channels or structural lattices, the geometry remains manifold, watertight, and immediately fabricatable.

## **2\. Technical Approach and Innovation**

### **2.1 Agentic AI Swarm & Stagnation-Escape Framework**

ScanIQ couples its implicit voxel kernel with an agentic AI swarm designed to autonomously navigate competing structural, hydrodynamic, and thermal constraints. However, unguided AI optimization frequently encounters a fundamental mathematical limitation: algorithmic convergence plateaus, trapping the model in local minima where minor parameter mutations yield diminishing returns.  
To overcome this, ScanIQ introduces an operational "Human-in/on-the-Loop" stagnation-escape protocol:

> * **Plateau-for-K Metric:** The system continuously monitors objective function improvement across K consecutive generation cycles.  
> * **Delta-on-Objective Trigger:** When variance drops below a predefined threshold, the automated loop triggers a pause, surfacing the multi-variable parameter state to human engineers.  
> * **Targeted Override:** Domain experts inject strategic design intents or constraints, breaking the local minimum and empowering the AI swarm to resume high-velocity convergence toward globally optimal geometries.

### **2.2 Algorithmic Validation: The 17.4-Degree Logarithmic Spiral Drive**

The core computational framework has been rigorously validated through the generative design of a specialized toroidal drive system. The internal fluid acceleration paths and electromagnetic containment vanes are governed by precise logarithmic spiral mathematics:  
r(\\theta) \= a e^{b\\theta}  
Where the spiral pitch is mathematically locked at 17.4^\\circ, governed by the pitch coefficient \\tan(17.4^\\circ), ensuring optimal fluid pressure management and mitigation of micro-cavitation. The voxel engine programmatically unions housing lattices, subtracts fluid channels, and executes precise offset subtractions (0.15\\,\\text{mm} safety margins) for neodymium Halbach array vane configurations—all while maintaining a sub-0.05\\,\\text{mm} datum tolerance threshold.

### **2.3 Secure Execution & Parameter Mutation Layer**

To ensure industrial reliability and regulatory compliance (e.g., AMA Supercross structural standards), ScanIQ implements a Roslyn-sandboxed execution layer. This secure architecture allows the agentic swarm to dynamically generate and test C\# geometric subroutines within strict safety boundaries before passing validated models to additive or subtractive manufacturing pipelines.

## **3\. Phase I R\&D Plan and Milestones**

The proposed Phase I project is structured into four core technical objectives executed over a six-month R\&D timeline:

### **Task 1: High-Throughput Ingestion & Adaptive Voxel Resolution**

> * **Objective:** Develop high-performance voxel ingestion pipelines capable of processing multi-point dRGB and time-of-flight sensor data.  
> * **Success Metric:** Seamless ingestion and voxelization of complex scanning data at a 0.3\\,\\text{mm} resolution field, guaranteeing zero non-manifold artifacts across continuous internal geometries.

### **Task 2: Multi-Physics Agentic Optimization Engine**

> * **Objective:** Program the AI swarm architecture to autonomously execute complex morphological sequences (erode, dilate, Boolean subtract) targeting fluid acceleration and structural load paths under simulated operating loads.  
> * **Success Metric:** Autonomous generation of a fully validated, watertight solid assembly matching target hydrodynamic performance parameters within 50 computation cycles.

### **Task 3: Subsystem-Level Stagnation-Escape Protocol Integration**

> * **Objective:** Operationalize the plateau-for-K metric and delta-on-objective trigger within the agentic feedback loop.  
> * **Success Metric:** Successful detection of algorithmic stagnation and seamless execution of human-in-the-loop parameter overrides during benchmark component generation runs.

### **Task 4: Secure Sandbox & Production Export Pipeline**

> * **Objective:** Finalize the Roslyn-sandboxed C\# execution layer and optimize high-resolution mesh generation for direct 3MF and STL export.  
> * **Success Metric:** Flawless compilation and export of production-ready manufacturing files maintaining sub-0.05\\,\\text{mm} datum error.

## **4\. Commercialization Strategy**

ScanIQ targets the multi-billion-dollar high-performance powersports, aftermarket motocross, and specialized subsea propulsion manufacturing sectors. Currently, designing custom, race-winning suspension components and fluid-handling assemblies relies on slow, expensive trial-and-error prototyping.  
Our commercial entry point focuses on the extreme-performance aftermarket and specialized OEM sector, where rapid customization, strict tolerances, and exceptional strength-to-weight ratios are paramount. By compressing the design-to-manufacture cycle for complex geometries from weeks to minutes, ScanIQ unlocks unprecedented design freedom.  
Commercial validation is anchored by formal R\&D commitment letters secured from industry leaders **MX6 Racing** and **Stapes Performance**, providing real-world telemetry data, workflow observation sites, and direct field-testing channels. ScanIQ will monetize through a software-as-a-service (SaaS) and computational job-tier licensing model.

## **5\. Company, Facilities, and Team**

ScanIQ LLC is a Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) positioned at the forefront of computational manufacturing and artificial intelligence.

> * **Jacqueline Anderson (Founder, CEO, and Majority Owner):** Directs corporate strategy, scientific direction, and field telemetry collection, bridging high-stress mechanical environments with rigorous data acquisition methodologies.  
> * **Technical Lead & Engineering Architecture:** Directs core computative engineering architecture, implicit voxel mathematics development, and agentic swarm optimization pipelines.

Supported by strategic R\&D partnerships with MX6 Racing and Stapes Performance, ScanIQ possesses the technical excellence, software architecture expertise, and industry access required to successfully execute this Phase I SBIR project and commercialize the platform.

Algorithmic Synthesis and Computational Engineering Framework for Motocross Rear Shock Bodies Using PicoGK

Computational engineering represents a fundamental paradigm shift in high-performance racing component development. Rather than manually manipulating Boundary Representation (B-Rep) surfaces within traditional computer-aided design environments, physical components are synthesized algorithmically through code-driven implicit geometry engines. For high-stress motocross suspension components—specifically rear shock absorber bodies operating on 250cc and 450cc competition motorcycles such as Kawasaki KX250 and KX450 platforms utilizing 50mm Showa and KYB shock architectures—algorithmic design enables dynamic wall-thickness profiling, topological load-path alignment, and aggressive surface area scaling for thermal management. 

This report establishes a comprehensive computational engineering framework for parameterizing, modeling, and optimizing an additive-manufactured motocross rear shock body within the PicoGK (Pico Geometry Kernel) and LEAP71 ShapeKernel environment in C\#. 

Structural Kinematics, Pressure Dynamics, and Thermal Load Requirements

Motocross rear shock absorber bodies operate under severe, coupled mechanical, hydraulic, and thermal stress profiles. During high-speed competition, the rear suspension system experiences rapid cyclic impacts caused by terrain irregularities, square-edge bumps, and extreme landing forces following high-amplitude jumps.

Hydraulic Pressure Envelope and Wall Stress Distribution

Modern 50mm damper bodies house an internal cylinder bore of 50.0\\text{ mm} paired with an 18.0\\text{ mm} damper shaft. The internal fluid volume is divided into the main dampening cylinder and an auxiliary piggyback reservoir housing a flexible bladder pressurized with static nitrogen gas between 1.0\\text{ MPa} and 1.2\\text{ MPa} (145\\text{--}175\\text{ psi}). During high-velocity compression strokes, the displacement of the shock shaft forces hydraulic fluid through internal shims and compression valve orifices into the piggyback reservoir, inducing transient internal hydraulic pressure spikes ranging from 20.0\\text{ MPa} to 35.0\\text{ MPa}.

**STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP AND FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT**

*By and between Platinum Eagle Aerospace and ScanIQ LLC*

This Strategic Partnership and Framework Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into and effective as of **July 22, 2026** (the “Effective Date”), by and between:

**Platinum Eagle Aerospace Inc.,** a Florida corporation, with its principal place of business at 2200 N Commerce Pkwy \#200, Weston, FL 33326 (“**Platinum Eagle”** or “PEA”); and

**ScanIQ LLC,** a limited liability company \[organized under the laws of the State of \[STATE\]\], together with its principals and members **John Antaramian** and **Jacqueline Anderson**, with a principal address at 72382 Ridgecrest Ln, Palm Desert, CA 92260 (collectively, “**ScanIQ”**).

Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ are each referred to as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” John Antaramian and Jacqueline Anderson join this Agreement individually for purposes of the confidentiality, intellectual property assignment, non-competition, and representation provisions applicable to them.

# **Recitals**

**Whereas,** ScanIQ has developed and owns proprietary scanning and detection technology, know-how, trade secrets, software, designs, data, and one or more filed patent applications and/or issued patents (collectively, the “ScanIQ Technology” and “ScanIQ IP”);

**Whereas,** Platinum Eagle possesses aerospace expertise, capital, facilities, personnel, industry relationships, and other resources that can accelerate the development, refinement, and commercialization of the ScanIQ Technology across applicable industries;

**Whereas,** Platinum Eagle is participating in the ScanIQ business and the Group by contributing its experience and resources, and this partnership relates solely to ScanIQ, the Group entities, and the ScanIQ IP — it does not, and is not intended to, give ScanIQ, John Antaramian, or Jacqueline Anderson any ownership of, interest in, or claim to Platinum Eagle Aerospace Inc., its separate business, assets, or intellectual property;

**Whereas,** the Parties desire to form a fifty-fifty (50/50) partnership with respect to ScanIQ, its business, and the ScanIQ IP, and to establish a structured group of entities to hold intellectual property, own the operating business, and hold equity;

**Whereas,** this Agreement is intended to be the first, foundational contract between the Parties, to be followed by definitive entity formation documents, operating/shareholder agreements, and intellectual property assignments consistent with the terms set out herein;

**Now, therefore,** in consideration of the mutual promises and covenants set forth below, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

# **1\.  Definitions**

**(a)**  “ScanIQ IP” means all intellectual property owned, controlled, or developed by ScanIQ, John Antaramian, and/or Jacqueline Anderson relating to the ScanIQ Technology, including all patents and patent applications (whether filed, pending, provisional, or issued), inventions, trade secrets, know-how, software (source and object code), algorithms, designs, schematics, data, databases, models, prototypes, trademarks, domain names, copyrights, and all associated goodwill and rights to sue for past infringement.

**(b)**  “IP Holding Company” means the new entity to be formed under Section 3 to own and hold all ScanIQ IP and all future IP, and which is intended to remain separate and free-standing at all times.

**(c)**  “Parent Company” means the new Delaware holding corporation to be formed under Section 3 to issue equity (stock) and to own the Operating Company.

**(d)**  “Operating Company” means the new entity to be formed under Section 3 to conduct the operations and commercial business of ScanIQ, and which will be wholly owned by the Parent Company.

**(e)**  “Group” means, collectively, ScanIQ LLC, the IP Holding Company, the Parent Company, and the Operating Company.

**(f)**  “Board” means the single, unified board of directors/managers described in Section 5 that governs all entities in the Group.

**(g)**  “Confidential Information” has the meaning given in Section 8\.

# **2\.  Partnership and 50/50 Ownership of Existing Company**

**(a)**  The Parties hereby form a strategic partnership under which Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ shall be equal fifty percent (50%) / fifty percent (50%) partners in the existing ScanIQ LLC, its business, and all ScanIQ IP, including all filed and issued patents.

**(b)**  Promptly following the Effective Date, the Parties shall amend ScanIQ LLC's operating agreement (and cause any necessary transfers) so that ownership and all economic and voting rights in ScanIQ LLC are held 50% by Platinum Eagle and 50% by ScanIQ, with the ScanIQ 50% held equally by John Antaramian and Jacqueline Anderson (i.e., twenty-five percent (25%) of the total each).

**(c)**  The 50/50 ownership principle shall carry through to each new entity formed under this Agreement, such that Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ each hold an equal one-half interest at the ultimate ownership level, subject to the specific structure in Section 3\.

**(d)  No rights in Platinum Eagle Aerospace.** For the avoidance of doubt, this partnership relates only to ScanIQ, the Group entities, and the ScanIQ IP. Neither ScanIQ LLC, John Antaramian, nor Jacqueline Anderson acquires, or shall have, any ownership interest, equity, membership, shareholding, license, lien, or other right or claim in or to Platinum Eagle Aerospace Inc., or to its separate business, assets, personnel, facilities, contracts, relationships, intellectual property, or other property (collectively, the “Platinum Eagle Assets”). Platinum Eagle is participating in the ScanIQ business by contributing its experience and resources; all Platinum Eagle Assets, including any pre-existing or independently developed intellectual property of Platinum Eagle, remain the sole and exclusive property of Platinum Eagle. Platinum Eagle's contribution of access to its resources under Section 6 does not transfer ownership of, or grant any continuing right to, any Platinum Eagle Assets, except as Platinum Eagle may expressly agree in a separate signed writing. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to make Platinum Eagle a partner of, or to give the Group or ScanIQ any interest in, Platinum Eagle's own business.

# **3\.  Formation of New Entities and Structure**

As soon as reasonably practicable after the Effective Date, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to form and organize the following entities, each owned on a 50/50 basis between Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ (directly or indirectly):

**(a)  IP Holding Company.** A new entity that will own and hold all ScanIQ IP and all future intellectual property, patents, and patent filings of the Group. The IP Holding Company shall be, and shall at all times remain, separate, free-standing, and independent from the operating and parent entities, and shall not be merged into, or made a subsidiary of, the Parent Company or the Operating Company.

**(b)  Parent Company (Delaware).** A new holding corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware for the purpose of issuing equity (stock) to the owners and holding the Operating Company. The Parent Company shall own one hundred percent (100%) of the Operating Company.

**(c)  Operating Company.** A new entity that will conduct the day-to-day operations, development, manufacturing, sales, and commercialization of the ScanIQ Technology and business. The Operating Company shall be wholly owned by the Parent Company.

**(d)  Ownership of the new entities.** Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ shall each own fifty percent (50%) of the Parent Company (and thereby, indirectly, of the Operating Company) and fifty percent (50%) of the IP Holding Company. As between John Antaramian and Jacqueline Anderson, the ScanIQ 50% share shall be held equally, i.e., twenty-five percent (25%) of the total each.

**(e)  Separateness covenant.** The Parties covenant that the IP Holding Company will remain a distinct legal entity with its own books, records, and governance, and that its ownership of the ScanIQ IP will not be pledged, encumbered, transferred, or subordinated to the Operating Company or Parent Company except by unanimous written approval of the Board. The Operating Company will use the ScanIQ IP under a written license from the IP Holding Company on arm's-length terms approved by the Board.

**(f)  Definitive documents.** The specific form of each entity (LLC or corporation), its jurisdiction, tax elections, and the license terms between the IP Holding Company and the Operating Company shall be set out in definitive formation and governance documents consistent with this Agreement, to be prepared with the advice of counsel and tax advisors.

# **4\.  Contribution and Assignment of IP and Assets**

**(a)**  Upon formation of the new entities, John Antaramian, Jacqueline Anderson, and ScanIQ LLC shall assign, transfer, convey, and deliver to the appropriate entity all right, title, and interest in and to the ScanIQ IP and all related assets, with all ScanIQ IP (including all filed and issued patents) transferred to the IP Holding Company, and all operating assets transferred to the Operating Company.

**(b)**  Each of John Antaramian and Jacqueline Anderson agrees to execute and deliver all patent assignments, IP assignments, bills of sale, and other instruments, and to take all further actions, reasonably necessary to vest ownership of the ScanIQ IP and assets in the applicable entity and to record such assignments with the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office and any other applicable registry.

**(c)**  Platinum Eagle shall make the contributions of capital, resources, and services described in Section 6 in consideration for its 50% ownership.

**(d)**  The specific IP, patents, patent applications, and assets to be assigned are or will be listed on Exhibit A, which the Parties shall complete and attach prior to or at the time of transfer.

# **5\.  Governance and Unified Board**

**(a)  Single unified Board.** The Group shall be governed by a single, unified Board that serves as the board of directors or managers of every entity in the Group. The same individuals shall constitute the Board of ScanIQ LLC, the IP Holding Company, the Parent Company, and the Operating Company.

**(b)  Composition.** The Board shall include John Antaramian and Jacqueline Anderson, together with the member(s) designated by Platinum Eagle (the Platinum Eagle board designees). The total number of seats and each side's number of designees shall be set so as to preserve the equal-rights principle in subsection (c).

**(c)  Equal voting rights.** All Board members shall have equal voting rights on all decisions concerning the company and the Group. No member or side shall have a controlling, tie-breaking, or super-vote, and no action of the Board shall be taken except by the required vote of members holding equal votes, so that Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ maintain equal governance authority.

**(d)  Major decisions.** The following actions require approval of the Board (and, where they affect the fundamental structure or the ScanIQ IP, unanimous written approval): any sale, merger, dissolution, or recapitalization; any transfer, license, pledge, or encumbrance of ScanIQ IP or patents; admission of new owners; issuance of equity; incurrence of material debt; adoption of budgets; entry into material contracts; and any release or disclosure of Confidential Information under Section 8\.

**(e)  Meetings and consent.** The Board shall meet regularly and may act by unanimous or majority written consent as provided in the definitive governance documents. Each entity shall keep minutes and records of Board actions.

# **6\.  Resources and Development Commitments**

**(a)  Platinum Eagle contributions.** Platinum Eagle shall provide the Group with access to its resources to help develop the ScanIQ Technology and business, which may include capital, funding, engineering and technical personnel, facilities and equipment, testing capabilities, aerospace and industry expertise, manufacturing support, and business development and customer relationships. The specific resources, funding commitments, and milestones may be detailed in Exhibit B or a separate resource schedule approved by the Board.

**(b)  ScanIQ commitments.** ScanIQ, John Antaramian, and Jacqueline Anderson shall continue to develop, refine, and perfect the ScanIQ Technology for all applicable and applied industries, and shall devote the effort, know-how, and cooperation reasonably necessary to advance the Group's business.

**(c)  Good faith.** Each Party shall act in good faith and use commercially reasonable efforts to advance the purposes of the partnership and the success of the Group.

# **7\.  Equity, Capital, and Distributions**

**(a)**  Profits, losses, and distributions of each entity shall be shared equally (50/50) between Platinum Eagle and ScanIQ, subject to the entity's governance documents and applicable tax and legal requirements.

**(b)**  Additional capital contributions, if any, shall be made only as approved by the Board, and the Parties shall address in the definitive documents the treatment of any disproportionate contributions (e.g., dilution, loans, or preferred returns).

**(c)**  The Parent Company's capitalization (authorized and issued stock) shall be structured to reflect the 50/50 ownership and the governance terms of this Agreement.

# **8\.  Confidentiality and Non-Disclosure**

This Section 8 is intended to be a strong, binding non-disclosure obligation and is a material inducement to each Party entering into this Agreement.

**(a)  Definition.** “Confidential Information” means all non-public information of or relating to the Group, the ScanIQ Technology, the ScanIQ IP, patents and patent strategy, inventions, trade secrets, source code, algorithms, designs, data, financials, business plans, customers, suppliers, methods, and any other proprietary or company-secret information, in any form, whether or not marked confidential.

**(b)  Obligation.** Each Party and each individual signatory shall hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence, shall use it solely for the purposes of the Group and this Agreement, and shall not, at any time, disclose, release, divulge, publish, or make available any Confidential Information or data to any person or entity without the prior written approval of the Board.

**(c)  No disclosure without Board approval.** At no time shall any Confidential Information, proprietary information, or company secret be released or divulged to anyone — including employees, contractors, advisors, investors, or third parties — without the written approval of the Board. Where disclosure to a permitted recipient is approved, it shall be made only under a written confidentiality agreement at least as protective as this Section.

**(d)  Compelled disclosure.** If a Party is legally compelled to disclose Confidential Information, it shall, to the extent legally permitted, give prompt notice to the Board and cooperate to seek protective treatment, and shall disclose only the portion legally required.

**(e)  Exclusions.** Confidential Information does not include information that is or becomes public through no breach of this Agreement, was rightfully known without confidentiality obligation before disclosure, or is independently developed without use of Confidential Information — the burden of proving an exclusion resting on the Party asserting it.

**(f)  Trade secrets and survival.** The obligations of this Section survive termination of this Agreement indefinitely and, with respect to trade secrets, for so long as the information remains a trade secret under applicable law.

**(g)  Injunctive relief.** The Parties agree that a breach of this Section would cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages are inadequate, and that the non-breaching Party and the Group are entitled to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy, without the necessity of posting bond.

**(h)  Return of materials.** Upon request of the Board or termination, each person shall return or destroy all Confidential Information in its possession and certify such return or destruction.

# **9\.  Intellectual Property Ownership Going Forward**

**(a)**  All intellectual property, inventions, and improvements conceived or developed in connection with the Group's business, whether by a Party, an individual signatory, or Group personnel, shall be owned by the IP Holding Company and shall be subject to the same 50/50 ownership and separateness principles set out in this Agreement.

**(b)**  Each individual signatory hereby agrees to a present assignment of, and to promptly disclose and assign, all such future IP to the IP Holding Company, and to assist with patent prosecution and enforcement at the Group's expense.

**(c)**  The IP Holding Company shall remain the sole owner of the ScanIQ IP; the Operating Company's rights shall arise only under the Board-approved license referenced in Section 3(e).

# **10\.  Representations and Warranties**

**(a)**  Each Party represents that it has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and that this Agreement is binding and enforceable against it.

**(b)**  ScanIQ, John Antaramian, and Jacqueline Anderson represent that they own or control the ScanIQ IP, that to their knowledge the ScanIQ IP does not infringe the rights of any third party, and that the ScanIQ IP is not subject to any undisclosed lien, license, or encumbrance that would prevent the transfers contemplated by this Agreement.

**(c)**  Each Party represents that its entry into this Agreement does not conflict with any other agreement to which it is bound.

# **11\.  Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation**

**(a)**  During the term of the partnership and for sixty (60) months thereafter, no Party or individual signatory shall, without Board approval, engage in or assist a business that competes with the ScanIQ Technology or the Group's business, or use the ScanIQ IP or Confidential Information outside the Group.

**(b)**  During the same period, no Party shall solicit for hire the Group's employees or contractors, or solicit the Group's customers or suppliers to divert business away from the Group.

**(c)**  The Parties agree these restrictions are reasonable; if a court finds any restriction overbroad, it shall be enforced to the maximum extent permitted by law.

# **12\.  Transfer Restrictions**

**(a)**  No Party may sell, assign, pledge, or transfer its ownership interest in any Group entity, or the ScanIQ IP, without Board approval and without first offering the interest to the other Party on the same terms (right of first refusal), except for transfers expressly permitted in the definitive governance documents.

**(b)**  Any attempted transfer in violation of this Section is void. The definitive documents may include customary tag-along, drag-along, and buy-sell provisions consistent with the 50/50 structure.

# **13\.  Deadlock Resolution**

Because governance is equal (50/50), the Parties shall include in the definitive documents a mechanism to resolve deadlocks, which may include escalation to the principals, non-binding mediation, appointment of a mutually agreed neutral advisor, or a buy-sell (“shotgun”) procedure. Pending resolution of a deadlock, the Group shall continue ordinary-course operations and shall not take any Major Decision under Section 5(d).

# **14\.  Term and Termination**

**(a)**  This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues until superseded by the definitive entity and governance documents or terminated as provided herein. The partnership itself is intended to be of indefinite duration.

**(b)**  This Agreement may be terminated by mutual written agreement of the Parties, or as otherwise provided in the definitive documents.

**(c)**  Sections 8 (Confidentiality), 9 (IP), 11 (Non-Competition), 15 (Indemnification), 16 (Dispute Resolution/Governing Law), and 17 (Miscellaneous) survive termination. The separateness of the IP Holding Company and the ownership of the ScanIQ IP survive and are not affected by termination of the operating relationship.

# **15\.  Indemnification**

Each Party shall indemnify and hold harmless the other Party and the Group from and against losses arising out of its breach of this Agreement, its breach of the representations and warranties herein, or its gross negligence or willful misconduct, subject to any limitations set out in the definitive documents.

# **16\.  Governing Law and Dispute Resolution**

**(a)  Governing law.** This Agreement is governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. The internal governance and formation of the Parent Company shall additionally be governed by Delaware law, and the IP Holding Company and Operating Company by the laws of their respective states of formation.

**(b)  Dispute resolution.** The Parties shall first attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute through negotiation between the principals, then through non-binding mediation. Any dispute not so resolved shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, seated in Broward County, Florida, before a single arbitrator, and judgment on the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or equitable relief (including under Section 8\) from a court located in Broward County, Florida, and the Parties consent to such venue.

**(c)  Attorneys' fees.** In any proceeding to enforce this Agreement, the prevailing Party shall be entitled to recover its reasonable attorneys' fees and costs.

# **17\.  Miscellaneous**

**(a)  Further assurances.** Each Party shall execute and deliver such further documents and take such further actions as are reasonably necessary to carry out this Agreement, including forming the entities and completing the IP assignments.

**(b)  Entire agreement.** This Agreement is the entire agreement between the Parties on its subject matter and supersedes all prior discussions. It is intended to be the first, foundational contract, to be implemented by the definitive documents contemplated herein.

**(c)  Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended only by a writing signed by both Parties.

**(d)  Assignment.** Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's written consent, except as expressly permitted herein.

**(e)  Notices.** Notices shall be in writing and delivered to the addresses set out above (for ScanIQ, also to johnantaramian@gmail.com and 305-741-2025) or such other address as a Party designates in writing.

**(f)  Severability.** If any provision is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in effect, and the unenforceable provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to be enforceable.

**(g)  Waiver.** No waiver is effective unless in writing, and no waiver of one breach waives any other.

**(h)  Relationship.** Except for the ownership and governance arrangements expressly created herein, nothing creates a general agency; no Party may bind another except as authorized by the Board.

**(i)  Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together constitute one instrument.

* **Operating Company** — runs operations; wholly owned by the Parent Company; licenses the ScanIQ IP from the IP Holding Company.
